events.title: The Buttonwood Agreement Launches Wall Street Trading
events.description: Twenty-four stockbrokers signed an agreement under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street in New York City. They pledged to trade securities only with one another and to charge set commissions. The pact became the foundation of what grew into the New York Stock Exchange.
events.significance: It created the organized securities market that grew into one of the most influential financial institutions in the world.

events.title: Norway Adopts Its Constitution
events.description: Norway's constitution was signed at Eidsvoll, and the country declared itself an independent kingdom. The union with Sweden that followed soon after did not erase the achievement. The document remains one of the oldest written constitutions still in use.
events.significance: Norwegians still celebrate May 17 as their national day, with parades and festivities across the country.

events.title: Brown v. Board of Education Decision
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled unanimously that racially segregated public schools are unconstitutional. The decision overturned the idea that separate facilities could be considered equal.
events.significance: The ruling became a legal cornerstone of the American civil rights movement, though putting it into practice took many years.

events.title: Senate Watergate Hearings Begin on Television
events.description: The U.S. Senate's special committee opened public hearings into the Watergate scandal, and the proceedings were televised. Millions of Americans watched testimony about political espionage and the efforts to cover it up.
events.significance: The hearings exposed abuses of power at the highest level and set in motion events that led to President Nixon's resignation in 1974.

events.title: WHO Removes Homosexuality from Its List of Mental Disorders
events.description: The World Health Organization's member states approved a revision that deleted homosexuality from the international classification of diseases.
events.significance: The decision marked a major shift in global medical views, and the date is now observed as the International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia.
